chunks.label: Walking and running
chunks.rationale: Say how you're getting somewhere on foot and tell someone to hurry.
chunks.interference: isogu is hurrying in general, not running; tobu covers both fly and jump.

chunks.label: On, off, open, close
chunks.rationale: Ask to switch lights and the AC on or off and to open or shut windows and doors.
chunks.interference: Lights and TVs take tsukeru and kesu, never akeru and shimeru.

chunks.label: Trains and buses
chunks.rationale: Get on, get off, change lines and grumble about the crowds.
chunks.interference: noru takes ni (densha ni noru) but oriru takes o (densha o oriru).

chunks.label: Hungry, thirsty, sleepy, drunk
chunks.rationale: Say how your body is doing right now.
chunks.interference: onaka suita and nodo kawaita are past forms but mean 'I'm hungry' and 'I'm thirsty' now.

chunks.label: Sitting and lining up
chunks.rationale: Handle seats, queues and crowds: sit, line up, meet up, move aside.
chunks.interference: narabu is joining a line yourself; atsumaru is people gathering as a group.

chunks.label: Morning routine
chunks.rationale: Talk through the start of a day: waking someone, washing, heading out, changing, going to school or work.
chunks.interference: okosu wakes someone else; waking up yourself is okiru.

chunks.label: Clothes and weight
chunks.rationale: Talk about what you wear, how it looks on you, and gaining or losing weight.
chunks.interference: futotta and yaseta are past forms used for how someone is now.

chunks.label: Cooking and clearing up
chunks.rationale: Make a meal and clear up: cut, get things ready, grill, throw out.
chunks.interference: kiru 'cut' (kirimasu) sounds like kiru 'wear' (kimasu); the forms tell them apart.

chunks.label: Laugh, sing, dance, kiss
chunks.rationale: Describe a fun night out or an affectionate moment.
chunks.interference: nameru also means 'look down on' (namenna yo!), unrelated to licking.

chunks.label: Sick days
chunks.rationale: Call in sick, say you've caught a cold and talk about getting better.
chunks.interference: naoru is the illness getting better; naosu is you curing it.

chunks.label: Falls and bumps
chunks.rationale: Describe small mishaps: getting soaked, collapsing, tripping, banging into things.
chunks.interference: korobu is tripping over; taoreru is collapsing or toppling.

chunks.label: Driving and stopping
chunks.rationale: Drive, give turns and say when something stops or won't move.
chunks.interference: tomaru and ugoku happen by themselves; doing it to something is tomeru and ugokasu.

chunks.label: Trips and moves
chunks.rationale: Talk about travel plans and moving: set off, move on, arrive, move house.
chunks.interference: idou suru is getting from place to place; hikkosu is moving house.

chunks.label: Taking people along
chunks.rationale: Bring or take a friend, child or pet, or ask to be picked up.
chunks.interference: tsurete kuru is toward the speaker, tsurete iku away; for things use motte kuru and motte iku.

chunks.label: Following and chasing
chunks.rationale: Follow, tag along, approach, chase or spot someone.
chunks.interference: tsuite kuru (follow me) and tsuite iku (I'll go with you) flip on direction, like kuru and iku.

chunks.label: Welcoming and guiding
chunks.rationale: Recognise 'come' in respectful, humble and parental speech, and offer to show someone around.
chunks.interference: irassharu raises the other person and mairu lowers yourself; never use irassharu for yourself.

drops.reason: Te-form of 急ぐ (same input romaji isogu); its use as 'Hurry!' is covered by that entry's example.
